rejected_titles: MSAA_4X_HINT causes SIGTRAP in the Metal-GL render pass on macOS (app ran 6s+ cleanly under timeout; not reproduced)
Restart (R key) aborts with SIGABRT (3 create/run/destroy cycles ran clean headlessly; allocator pollution real but crash not reproduced)
Dangling hint string SIGTRAPs next frame (UAF confirmed by code, crash not reproduced)
Reported '45 tests' is inaccurate (40 core + 5 app/run = 45, verified by running both suites)
E1 severance pin 'never puts a packet on the pipe' (occupied pin exists: on_pipe_count==0 tfails)

error404.log.bin identical to boot.log.bin 'despite diverging state' (both are seed-42 no-command runs; the log IS the input — identical inputs are correct; replay verified 250 ticks against its own manifest)
CI step labeled 'replay gate' never runs replay (verify_replay runs inside run_demo; CI harness.sh run exercises it)
CI never builds the gitignored software renderer (harness.sh builds the shadow when missing; I built it)
blind-a 'dist2/tier_index have no call sites' (chunk-limited; both are called in testkit/tests)

empirical.raylib_sw_shadow: built from source (raylib 6.0, PLATFORM_MEMORY + rlsw) and harness built against it

findings.title: Committed app.bin — a 2MB Mach-O arm64 build artifact tracked at the repo root
findings.evidence: git ls-files app.bin → tracked; file app.bin → 'Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64'; .gitignore has bin/ but not app.bin; PR body never mentions app.bin; diff shows 'app.bin | Bin 0 -> 2057480 bytes'
findings.detail: Platform-specific build artifact (2MB) churns on every rebuild, bloats the repo, and is not declared deliberate anywhere in the PR description or Decisions section.
findings.recommended_fix: git rm --cached app.bin, add 'app.bin' to .gitignore, push the removal commit. CI builds from source (odin build app).

findings.title: Left-click can never select a pipe, open the pipe popover, or dismiss an open popover — demolish is UI-dead and full routers soft-lock
findings.evidence: handle_click_select is called only inside 'if rl.IsMouseButtonReleased(.LEFT) && app.drag.active'; app.drag.active is set only when the press landed on a node ('if nid, ok := prun.snap_node(...); ok { ... app.drag.active = true }'). Presses on pipes/empty ground never set it, so the release branch (and with it pipe select, app.sel={} dismissal, and the demolish button in popover_click) is unreachable.
findings.detail: Mouse-only prototype: pipes cannot be selected (right-click still cycles priority; router select works), popovers cannot be dismissed by clicking away (ESC works), and demolish — the GDD's 'redesign is the game' verb and the only way to free ports/budget — is unreachable, so a full router is a permanent dead end.
findings.recommended_fix: Run handle_click_select on every left release regardless of drag.active (or set drag.active=true on any press), keeping the draw path gated on press_node != 0.

findings.title: T1 state fingerprint omits Health_Meter.in_breach and .healthy_streak despite 'covers ALL sim state' claim
findings.evidence: state_writer writes meter_pct, grace_ticks_left, in_grace, won, lost, surge_delivered, surge_dropped, prev_in_surge — but not h.in_breach nor h.healthy_streak; both gate future behavior (E30 hysteresis band, grace-refill streak). Header comment: 'covers ALL sim state'.
findings.detail: A divergence in those two fields would go unseen by goldens/replay until it leaks into hashed meter/grace/event fields (within a tick or two in practice). Spine verified intact empirically (3000+250 ticks bit-for-bit), so this is a fingerprint-completeness gap, not a live determinism break.
findings.recommended_fix: Add w_bool(&w, h.in_breach); w_bool(&w, h.healthy_streak); then deliberately re-bless goldens (harness save).

findings.title: E7 WRR-floor test is vacuous — weights {100,1,1} exceed MAX_WEIGHT=64, are silently rejected, and the zero-share premise never holds
findings.evidence: validate_command: 'if c.weights[0] > MAX_WEIGHT ... return .Invalid_Weights'; submit_c: 'if err == .None { state.budget = nb }' — the {100,1,1} command is dropped; the pipe keeps default weights so Standard gets a share and the test passes for the wrong reason.
findings.detail: The E7 1-unit quantum floor is implemented in advance() but is not pinned by any test — a regression would pass CI. The test comment claims 'Standard gets cap 0 by allocation' which never happens.
findings.recommended_fix: Use weights within MAX_WEIGHT that still round Standard to 0 (e.g. {64,1,1} on a 5-capacity narrow pipe), or call qos_allocate directly.

findings.title: Severance-reroute test cannot distinguish reroute-survival from fresh-spawn deliveries — the captured drop counter is discarded
findings.evidence: sev_drops_before is captured ('sev_drops_before := state.flow.sla[streaming].dropped') then discarded ('_ = sev_drops_before'); the assertion is only 'del_after <= del_before → tfail', which 30/tick fresh spawns satisfy regardless of whether any mid-edge packet survived the reroute.
findings.detail: E1 branch-1 (reroute survival) is claimed as pinned but only proves deliveries continue. The drop-branch test (no alternative) is sound.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert on the severance-tagged drop count staying ~0 with an alternative (and reroute-sourced deliveries), not on raw delivered totals.

findings.title: Node-health warning surface (Strained/Critical, Ev_Warning_Raised/Cleared) has zero test coverage
findings.location: core/crisis.odin:crisis_evaluate (no crisis_test.odin exists; no demo asserts Warning_Raised)
findings.evidence: ls core/*crisis* → only crisis.odin; grep Warning_Raised core/*_test.odin demos/*.dem → no hits; surge_basics.dem asserts forecast/crisis/run_won, error404.dem asserts grace/run_lost — neither asserts the 🟡/🔴 warning events.
findings.detail: The primary warning surface (GDD M5, 'I should have seen this coming') is exercised only transitively through goldens. Godot r1 flagged the same gap ('node_health_states untested'); the lesson was not applied.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a crisis_test.odin: drive node_load over thresholds, assert Warning_Raised/Cleared transitions and the Strained→Critical ordering.

findings.title: Queue-overflow shed (queue_drop_depth, newest-first) and the E9 drop-ladder emptiness combos have no test
findings.location: core/flow.odin:advance (queue_drop_depth branch); no test references Queue_Overflow
findings.evidence: grep queue_drop_depth|Queue_Overflow core/*_test.odin → no hits; the shed branch ('if idx_in_lane > int(bal.queue_drop_depth) ... drop_packet(f, idx, .Queue_Overflow, ...)') is reachable only via catalog-patched fixtures, none of which exist.
findings.detail: The per-lane queue bound (the E22 backstop and the visible 'congestion piles' surface) is completely unpinned, including the newest-first shed order and the E9 ladder ordering.
findings.recommended_fix: Patch queue_drop_depth in a fixture (test_catalog_sources exists) and assert shed order BE→Standard→Express and newest-first semantics.

findings.title: Router triage popover labels are swapped: the 'stream' button sets triage=0 (email) and 'email' sets triage=1 (streaming)
findings.evidence: labels := [3]string{'none','stream','email'}; triage := i32(i - 1) → button 1 ('stream') sends triage=0; data/packet_types.json order is [0]=email, [1]=streaming. The draw side uses the same mapping, so the highlight is self-consistent but the semantics are inverted.
findings.detail: The differentiator surface (junction triage) labels the buttons opposite to the class they promote — a player clicking 'stream' makes email win contention.
findings.recommended_fix: Swap the label order to {'none','email','stream'}, or make triage = i with labels {'none','email','stream'} consistently in both files.

findings.title: context.allocator is left as the run arena after core.step() — snapshot arrays and later app allocations ride the run arena; restart leaks 16MB arena_buf
findings.location: core/run.odin:step ('context.allocator = state.allocator') never restores; app/run/run.odin:resnapshot→snapshot_write uses ambient context.allocator; run_context_destroy deletes arena_buf under the polluted allocator
findings.evidence: core/run.odin:112 'context.allocator = state.allocator'; snapshot_write appends use context.allocator (the passed allocator param is unused — blind-a note); run_context_destroy does 'delete(rc.arena_buf)' with the stale arena allocator (no-op → 16MB leak per R-key restart).
findings.detail: ODN-18 discipline violation with real consequences: cross-allocator delete (a no-op here, a crash under a tracking allocator), per-restart leaks, and the run arena growing with view traffic. My 3-cycle headless create→run→destroy test did not crash, so the SIGABRT claim is not reproduced — but the pollution is real.
findings.recommended_fix: Save/restore context.allocator around step() and pass explicit allocators to snapshot_write (make the param real). Delete arena_buf with the allocator that created it.

findings.title: Dangling hint string: fmt.tprintf results (temp arena) stored in app.hint are freed by free_all at the top of the next frame, then read for up to 2600ms
findings.location: app/main.odin:set_hint / cycle_priority ('set_hint(app, fmt.tprintf("%s gets the Express lane..."), frame_ms)') + main loop free_all(context.temp_allocator)
findings.evidence: main loop: 'free_all(context.temp_allocator) // frame arena discipline (ODN-18)' at top of every frame; set_hint stores the tprintf pointer; draw_frame reads app.hint while frame_ms <= app.hint_until (2600ms TTL).
findings.detail: Use-after-free on the QoS-toast path — the string's memory is reused next frame. On this machine the app did not SIGTRAP (temp arena stays mapped), but the displayed text is garbage-or-stale and a tracking build could fault.
findings.recommended_fix: Copy the hint into app-owned storage (fixed [256]u8 buffer) instead of storing the temp-arena slice.

findings.title: harness save silently blesses demos whose expectations/intents FAILED — exits 0 and prints 'blessed'
findings.location: harness/main.odin:run_demo ('return ok || save') + main save branch
findings.evidence: 'ok := len(fail_msgs) == 0 ... return ok || save'; main: 'if failures > 0 { ... os.exit(1) } ... fmt.printf("harness: blessed %d demo(s)\n", ...)' — with save=true the function returns true even when expectations failed, so failures stays 0.
findings.detail: A re-bless can mask a broken demo (missing event, wrong terminal state) while printing success — the 'save is deliberate, PR-reviewed' doctrine (§10.6) is undercut by the tool itself.
findings.recommended_fix: In save mode, still write goldens but exit non-zero (or print FAIL loudly) when fail_msgs is non-empty; require --force to bless a failing demo.

findings.title: 'demolish node' with no name reads fields[2] out of bounds — harness panics instead of returning a parse error
findings.evidence: 'case "demolish": if len(fields) < 2 { return ... }; if fields[1] == "node" { it.verb = "demolish_node"; it.a = strings.clone(fields[2]) }' — 'demolish node' alone passes the len<2 guard and indexes fields[2].
findings.detail: Malformed demo input crashes the harness instead of failing cleanly with a line-numbered parse error; the parse-error contract is broken.
findings.recommended_fix: Guard: if fields[1] == 'node' && len(fields) < 3 { return it, parse error }.

findings.title: save_diff_bundle hands Odin temp-arena memory to raylib's UnloadImage (cross-allocator free) on the T2-mismatch diagnostic path
findings.evidence: out := make([]rl.Color, n, context.temp_allocator); dimg.data = raw_data(out); ... rl.ExportImage(dimg, ...); rl.UnloadImage(dimg) — raylib frees the temp-arena buffer with its own allocator.
findings.detail: Undefined behavior exactly when the harness is most needed (a pixel mismatch): the diff-bundle path frees foreign memory. It is why the T2 failure path can SIGABRT instead of producing a diff.
findings.recommended_fix: Export first, then delete(out) with the Odin allocator and skip rl.UnloadImage (or allocate via RL allocator APIs).

findings.title: crises.json is parsed and hashed but its fields are never consumed — tuning it forces a golden re-bless with zero behavior change
findings.location: core/catalog.odin:315-334 (parse) vs core/crisis.odin (engine hardcodes root cause; no reader of preventive_redesign/lead_time/failure_effect)
findings.evidence: grep preventive_redesign|lead_time_ticks|failure_effect core/*.odin app/*.odin → only catalog.odin (parse). crisis.odin hardcodes 'rc := Root_Cause{pattern = .No_Spare_Capacity_For_Forecast_Spike, node = 0}' and derives surge timing from demand.json.
findings.detail: The fairness contract's 'structured root cause + preventive redesign' (FORGE #3) is hardcoded, and the catalog entry is dead weight that silently invalidates goldens (catalog_hash) when edited.
findings.recommended_fix: Either consume crises.json (look up the archetype's root_cause/preventive_redesign into the event) or delete the catalog until it is real — a parsed-but-unconsumed file is a trap.

findings.title: Committed self-review docs (verification-gap.md, edge-case-hunter.md) describe a pre-fix codebase — their headline blockers are false at the reviewed sha
findings.evidence: verification-gap.md:403 'no step runs odin build app' — ci.yml:47 DOES 'odin build app'; verification-gap.md:214-242 'upgrade path is unreachable from demos' — draw_and_upgrade.dem uses upgrade_pipe and passes; edge-case-hunter.md W1 'E30 hysteresis has no catalog fields' — balance.json ships breach_exit_pct:93.
findings.detail: Five lenses independently flagged the same staleness: the fixes were applied but the committed review reports still grade the pre-fix state, so a fresh minion reading them would chase ghosts.
findings.recommended_fix: Update or remove the committed review docs so they describe the reviewed commit; note in the PR that they predate the final fixes.

findings.title: Catalog loader silently truncates i64→i32 and accepts unknown keys — ODN-5 fail-fast contract unmet
findings.evidence: jint: 'case json.Integer: return i32(x)' — direct truncation; u64 tick fields ride through 'u64(jint(...))' (i64→i32→u64 wrap); unknown keys are never enumerated/rejected despite ODN-5: 'unknown fields, out-of-range values ... abort startup with a named error'.
findings.detail: Latent: current catalog values are small so nothing truncates today, but a tick or multiplier beyond i32 silently corrupts the sim — and goldens would re-bless the corruption.
findings.recommended_fix: jint64 for tick/count fields with range checks at load; enumerate expected keys and reject unknown ones per ODN-5.

findings.title: Zero-traffic neutral ticks (uptime -1) during an open breach still burn grace and drain the meter at MAXIMUM severity
findings.evidence: 'if recent_uptime < 0 { // neutral: no breach, no credit — but an open episode stays open }' then 'if h.in_breach { ... }' proceeds to decrement grace and, after expiry, 'severity := bal.win_uptime_pct - recent_uptime' → 90 - (-1) = 91 → drain = clamp(91/10, 1, max) = max. E24 says zero-demand = neutral.
findings.detail: A demand gap mid-episode drains the meter at the maximum per-tick rate — the opposite of E24's neutral intent, and unfair on the 'no phantom loss' contract.
findings.recommended_fix: In the neutral branch, skip grace decrement and drain (keep the episode open, hold state), or clamp recent_uptime to [0,100] before severity math.

findings.title: pick_dst allocates two dynamic arrays per spawned packet on the run arena — unbounded arena growth over a long run
findings.evidence: cand: [dynamic]u32; cand_w: [dynamic]i32; defer delete(cand); defer delete(cand_w) — per call, inside the per-packet spawn loop (flow_step calls pick_dst per packet); arena allocator free is a no-op, so the memory accumulates until run destroy.
findings.detail: ODN-18 'zero per-frame heap churn' is violated in the hottest path; at PROTO scale (hundreds of packets) the growth is small, but the pattern is wrong and scales badly.
findings.recommended_fix: Reuse persistent scratch buffers (like sc_src_ids) or a stack array for the ≤3-candidate case.

findings.title: nearest_pipe bezier hit-testing (the 0118cc0 flagship fix) has zero test coverage
findings.evidence: grep nearest_pipe app/ core/ → only snap.odin (def) + main.odin (callers); driver_test.odin tests snap_node inclusivity (:64-72) but nothing calls nearest_pipe.
findings.detail: The head commit's headline change — 'pipe hit-testing follows the rendered bezier' — is unpinned; a regression in the polyline sampling would ship silently.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a driver_test asserting nearest_pipe hits a point ON the bezier curve and misses a point on the chord-only path (> tolerance from the curve).

findings.title: Grace countdown computes ticks×hz (inverted), discards it, and renders a static '!' — the countdown numeral never appears
findings.evidence: secs := snap.grace_ticks_left * i32(v.catalogs.balance.logic_hz)  (should be ÷); _ = secs; txt := fmt_bprintf(buf[:], "!", 0) — the computed seconds are discarded and a literal '!' is drawn.
findings.detail: The HUD grace countdown — the player's telegraph for the loss timer — is dead code drawing a static glyph; the architecture's 'grace countdown' visibility surface is absent.
findings.recommended_fix: secs := grace_ticks_left / logic_hz; fmt_bprintf(buf[:], "%ds", secs) and draw it.

findings.title: Grace-reset test passes even with the instant re-arm exploit it claims to pin — only the end state after 100 healthy ticks is asserted
findings.evidence: The test runs 100 healthy ticks then asserts grace_ticks_left == grace_window_ticks — under gradual refill (5/tick after a 50-tick streak) AND under instant re-arm, the end state is identical; no mid-stretch assertion exists.
findings.detail: The PR's claimed fix ('grace refills gradually ... closes the never-lose flapping exploit') is not pinned by this test; the exploit could return and CI would stay green.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert grace_ticks_left partway through the healthy stretch (e.g. at tick +60, grace must be < full), pinning the gradual refill.

findings.title: draw_and_reject.dem header claims ports + budget rejection classes but the script never triggers them
findings.evidence: Header: 'every rejection class returns its typed error (E3/E26 + span + ports + budget)'; script draws 6 pipes to the mid router (8 ports) and never approaches the 5200 budget — no Router_Ports_Full, no Over_Budget line exists.
findings.detail: The demo overclaims its coverage; the port-limit E2E rejection (canon #14) is asserted only by the unit test, and budget rejection has no E2E pin at all.
findings.recommended_fix: Either add the missing intent lines (fill a basic-4 router; draw until over budget) or fix the header to name what is actually exercised.

findings.title: upgrade_pipe accepts a silent downgrade — no tier-direction check; delta max(0,·)=0, no refund, no error
findings.evidence: validate checks span and delta cost only; apply: 'delta_cost := max(0, draw_cost(new) - draw_cost(old))' — a to_tier below the current tier passes validation with zero cost and lowers the pipe.
findings.detail: The demo grammar can downgrade for free (draw_and_upgrade.dem's narrow upgrade is rejected only on span, not direction). UI has no upgrade path in PROTO, so latent — but the sim contract is wrong.
findings.recommended_fix: Reject to_tier <= current tier in validate_command (.Tier_Downgrade), or implement deliberate downgrades with refund semantics.

findings.title: Standalone replay gate cannot detect a cross-wired log: manifest demo identity is parsed then discarded
findings.evidence: read_manifest parses the demo name into the manifest struct; verify_replay/run_replay never compare it to the requested demo; boot.log.bin and error404.log.bin are byte-identical (both seed-42 no-command logs) so cross-wiring them is undetectable.
findings.detail: For identical-input demos the logs ARE identical (correct — the log is the input), but the gate should still verify log↔manifest identity (seed, catalog_hash, logic_hz) to catch operator error.
findings.recommended_fix: In run_replay, compare manifest.seed/catalog_hash/logic_hz against the log header and the demo name against the manifest before hashing.

findings.title: error404's 8s T2 golden is byte-identical to boot's 1s golden — the drain phase is never visualized
findings.evidence: md5 match confirmed; the unwired loss path shows the same idle map + full meter at both times (drain begins only after grace expires at 20s; the 40s capture is the frozen terminal lockup).
findings.detail: T2 covers 'before' and 'terminal' but never the mid-drain meter — the visual telegraph of the loss condition has no pixel pin.
findings.recommended_fix: Capture a frame between grace expiry and terminal (e.g. 30000ms) so the partially drained meter is golden-pinned.

findings.title: 'expect hash stable' is declared by all 7 demos but the harness never evaluates it — the T1 compare runs unconditionally anyway
findings.location: harness/main.odin:run_demo (:299-300) — 'case .Hash_Stable: // the manifest compare below is the substance'
findings.evidence: The Expect_Kind.Hash_Stable case is an empty comment; check_hashes (the real T1 compare) runs for every demo regardless. So the expectation line is decorative, and hash-stability is actually stronger than declared (always on).
findings.detail: Misleading syntax, benign behavior — the demo language advertises a toggle that doesn't exist; a future author may assume removing the line disables the check.
findings.recommended_fix: Either evaluate the expectation explicitly or drop the keyword from the demo grammar documentation.

findings.title: Replay gate hardcodes bare=false — 'map bare' demos always replay against the six-node fixture
findings.evidence: verify_replay declares bar := false, discards it, and calls replay_hashes with a literal false — the fixture flag is dead code; a future bare demo would falsely fail (or falsely pass) the replay gate.
findings.detail: No bare demos ship today, so the gate is green — but the dead parameter is a latent trap for the next demo author.
findings.recommended_fix: Thread the demo's map_fixture into verify_replay/replay_hashes.

findings.title: state_dump, run_destroy, PCG32_INC, TICK_SECONDS are dead — defined, never referenced
findings.evidence: grep for each symbol outside its definition → no callers; run_destroy is superseded by arena teardown; TICK_SECONDS claims 'derived from balance.logic_hz' but the driver computes tick_seconds from the catalog and never reads the constant.
findings.detail: Four dead symbols, two with misleading comments — small maintenance noise; PCG32_INC's comment even claims a use that doesn't exist.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete or wire them; fix the comments.

findings.title: App mode/press_valid/cosmetic_rng fields are written, never read
findings.evidence: app.mode = .Boot / .Run set but never read (the run state gates via rc.paused/rc.ended); press_valid written at :197/:203, never read; cosmetic_rng seeded at :64, never drawn (map_gen uses its own stream).
findings.detail: ODN-13's mode FSM is vestigial — the game is a single Run mode; the cosmetic RNG (ODN-15) is declared but unused. Harmless, but misleading for future readers.
findings.recommended_fix: Remove or implement: either drive the FSM or delete mode; either draw cosmetic randomness or delete the field.

findings.title: Severance reroute keeps the old vis_q8 — a shorter new route can draw the packet at its destination (p.dst fallback)
findings.location: core/flow.odin:advance severance block (compute_route resets edge_idx/progress_units but not vis_q8) + core/snapshot.odin:packet_edge_pos fallback
findings.evidence: The severance branch calls compute_route then sets p.edge_idx = 0; p.progress_units = 0 — vis_q8 is untouched; packet_edge_pos returns p.dst when the Q8 fraction exceeds the route.
findings.detail: Cosmetic-only (vis_q8 is a deterministic Q8 position that rides the T1 hash), but a severed packet can visibly teleport to the destination. Determinism is unaffected.
findings.recommended_fix: Reset p.vis_q8 in the severance branch (e.g. vis_q8 = id%64*4*route_len, matching spawn).

findings.title: Action-log roundtrip test compares only 2 of 6 command kinds — the #partial switch silently skips the rest
findings.evidence: #partial switch ca in ka { case Cmd_Draw_Pipe: ... case Cmd_Set_Pipe_Priority: ... } — Upgrade/Demolish/Set_Lane_Weights/Set_Junction_Triage kinds are never round-tripped; a serialization bug in any of them passes.
findings.detail: The ODN-11 binary contract is pinned for 2 of 6 commands; the log reader's case coverage is exercised only by the corruption tests.
findings.recommended_fix: Exercise all six kinds in the roundtrip (a fixture log with one of each), or switch to an exhaustive switch.

findings.title: test_rng_streams_independent tests the opposite of its name — same seed reproducing the identical stream is the determinism keystone, not independence
findings.evidence: The test seeds a and b with 1337 and asserts rng_next(a) == rng_next(b) — that is stream identity, not independence; 'streams independent' (ODN-15's separate cosmetic stream) is untested.
findings.detail: Naming bug; the assertion itself is valuable (same-seed reproduction). Independence of two differently-seeded streams is trivially true but unpinned.
findings.recommended_fix: Rename to test_rng_same_seed_reproduces, and optionally add a different-seed divergence assert.

findings.title: submit_c swallows validation errors — fixture draws can silently no-op and tests pass on the wrong topology
findings.evidence: 'nb, _, err := topology_apply_edit(...); if err == .None { state.budget = nb }' — an invalid draw is dropped silently; callers never check. This is how the E7 test's {100,1,1} rejection went unnoticed.
findings.detail: Test-authoring footgun: a wrong tier/span in a fixture silently changes what the test exercises. Should fail loudly in test builds.
findings.recommended_fix: tfail on err != .None inside submit_c (or return the error and assert at call sites).

findings.title: check_golden leaks the captured frame image on both T2 failure branches
findings.evidence: UnloadImage(img) happens only in the else (match) branch; the no-golden and mismatch branches save_diff_bundle(img) then never unload img.
findings.detail: Small leak per failed capture on the diagnostic path — the path that matters most. Bounded per run, but trivially fixable.
findings.recommended_fix: rl.UnloadImage(img) before each return in check_golden.

findings.title: write_file and write_log are byte-identical duplicates; unreachable duplicate os.exists guard in check_golden
findings.evidence: Both procs are identical ('if err := os.write_entire_file(path, data); err != nil { fmt.eprintfln(...) }'); check_golden has 'if !os.exists(path) { ... }' followed by a second unreachable 'if !os.exists(path) { /* handled above */ }'.
findings.detail: Dedupe + dead code — maintenance noise in the harness's central file.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete write_log (alias write_file) and the second os.exists guard.

findings.title: raylib fetched by mutable tag (no commit pin/checksum); demo names interpolated into paths unsanitized
findings.evidence: 'git clone --depth 1 --branch "$RAYLIB_TAG" https://github.com/raysan5/raylib.git' — a tag, not a sha; golden_path/diff dirs embed the demo name from CLI args/dir listing without sanitization.
findings.detail: Tag-pinning is weaker than the 'pinned' language in §10.4; a tag force-push would change golden bytes. Demo-name path traversal is local-only (CLI user) — low risk, worth a guard.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin raylib to a commit sha + verify checksum in build_raylib_sw.sh; reject demo names containing '/' or '..'.

findings.title: fmt_bprintf/write_uint write past fixed stack buffers with no length guard; draw_forecast's [32] buffer needs 27 literal chars before the digits
findings.evidence: write_uint writes into buf[n:] with no bound check; '~%ds out - build capacity NOW' is 27 chars before the digits — a 5+-digit seconds value overflows the [32] buffer.
findings.detail: Latent stack overflow: secs = ticks_until/hz is bounded today (≤ 600 ticks lead), but the helper is unsafe by construction and one wide value smashes the stack.
findings.recommended_fix: Bounds-check n against len(buf) in write_uint/fmt_bprintf (clamp or return what fits).

findings.title: map_draw grid loops spin forever when tile == 0 (minimized-window state) — from_screen guards scale<=0 but the draw path doesn't
findings.evidence: tile := v.tile_px * v.scale; 'for x < f32(v.win_w) { ...; x += tile }' — with scale == 0 (0×0 window), x never advances. from_screen guards 'if v.scale <= 0 { return 0, 0 }' but map_draw has no such guard.
findings.detail: Minimizing the window to 0×0 on some platforms can hang the frame loop. main.odin:125 recomputes the view when scale==0 but only at frame start with the current window size.
findings.recommended_fix: Guard map_draw (and other draw paths) with scale > 0, or clamp view_compute's scale to a minimum.

findings.title: Catalog cross-checks omit a crises.json Surge entry; zero-terminal demand accrues with no Ev_Packet_Dropped; several parsed fields are never consumed
findings.location: core/catalog.odin (cross-ref block; :199-205 latency_tol_ms/max_loss_pct etc.) + core/flow.odin:flow_step zero-terminal branch
findings.evidence: crises load checks archetype non-empty but never verifies the engine's .Surge exists in the catalog; flow_step's 'len(src_ids) == 0' branch accrues drops with no event; latency_tol_ms, max_loss_pct, clean_span, shape, sla_fail_effect, era_introduced, demand_weight are parsed but never read.
findings.detail: PROTO-scoped dead catalog fields (documented [LATER] depth), but the missing Surge cross-check and eventless zero-terminal accrual are contract gaps (E28 event symmetry).
findings.recommended_fix: Add the Surge presence cross-check; emit Ev_Packet_Dropped{reason:.Unreachable} (or a volume-level event) in the zero-terminal branch.

findings.title: pipes_between returns a count beyond the scratch buffer; compute_route slices pair_buf[:cnt] out of bounds when a pair has >32 parallel pipes
findings.evidence: pipes_between counts ALL matches ('n += 1' after the write guard 'if n < len(out)'); compute_route does 'cnt := pipes_between(t, na, nb, pair_buf[:]); ... pick_pipe(f, t, na, nb, pair_buf[:cnt])' — cnt can exceed 32 and the slice panics.
findings.detail: Unreachable today: port limits cap parallel pipes at 16 per junction, terminals can't pair (E26), so no pair reaches 33. But the invariant is implicit — a port-limit change silently arms the panic.
findings.recommended_fix: Clamp cnt in compute_route (or have pipes_between return the written count when out is full).

findings.title: Snapshot is a bespoke per-tick projection, not ODN-1's SOA-memcpy double-buffer; packet storage is AoS [dynamic], not ODN-8's #soa pool + free list
findings.evidence: snapshot_write builds Snap_Node/Snap_Pipe/Snap_Packet arrays by field projection each tick; packets are a [dynamic]Packet with a per-tick survivor-copy compaction, not #soa[cap] + free list. Both are documented deviations in code comments and the PR body ('Routes inline [32]u32 per packet; ids monotonic u64 ... noted as a small deviation from ODN-8's slab sketch').
findings.detail: Declared deviations with determinism intact (arrays preserve insertion order; the projection is canonical-consistent). Perf/snapshot-lerp architecture is deferred — fine for PROTO, noted for the record.
findings.recommended_fix: None for PROTO — carry as documented debt; revisit at scale.

findings.title: Span/cost metric uses integer isqrt + round, where §6.1 pinned pure Euclidean² comparisons (no sqrt anywhere)
findings.evidence: span_between computes isqrt(d2) with round-half-up — the architecture says 'no sqrt anywhere in core' (Euclidean² comparisons only). The code comment justifies it: 'matches the proven-fun reference's round(sqrt(dx²+dy²))' — the Godot prototype used round(sqrt), and the Odin port reproduces its cost/span numbers.
findings.detail: Intentional deviation for behavioral parity with the reference; still integer-only and deterministic. Validation compares rounded span vs max_span — a pipe at 5.5 tiles rounds to 6, matching the reference's behavior.
findings.recommended_fix: None — document in the PR's decisions section (it is not currently listed there).

findings.title: Crisis root_cause is a hardcoded constant (node=0, pattern fixed) and the surge triggers on the catalog timeline, not measured strain
findings.evidence: 'rc := Root_Cause{pattern = .No_Spare_Capacity_For_Forecast_Spike, node = 0}; emit(... Ev_Crisis_Triggered{archetype = .Surge, set_piece = u16(i), root_cause = rc})' — fired when set_piece_active, regardless of measured load; per-node load IS measured in the same proc but never feeds the crisis decision.
findings.detail: The fairness contract's 'crisis traces to measurable strain' is structural for warnings (node health derives from load) but the surge itself is timeline-driven — which matches the GDD's forecast set-piece design. Root-cause attribution is placeholder.
findings.recommended_fix: PROTO-acceptable; when the remaining archetypes land, derive root_cause node from the measured strain locus.

findings.title: BFS neighbor buffer (64) silently drops neighbors beyond 64; no invariant enforces the 'nodes ≤ 64' assumption
findings.evidence: neighbors writes only while 'n < len(out)' and returns the capped count; compute_route's nb_buf[64] caps the BFS frontier silently — a node with >64 neighbors gets truncated routes (still deterministic, possibly suboptimal).
findings.detail: PROTO maps stay well under 64 nodes, so unreachable today; the buffer cap is an unstated invariant that would silently degrade routing at scale.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert or document the node-count invariant at spawn; size nb_buf from the topology.

findings.title: Set_Pipe_Priority / Set_Junction_Triage accept values below -1 as silent neutral; priority OOB reuses .Unknown_Command
findings.evidence: Cmd_Set_Pipe_Priority checks only 'c.priority >= i32(len(cat.packet_types))' — priority = -5 passes as neutral; Cmd_Set_Junction_Triage checks only the upper bound too.
findings.detail: Minor validation gap: out-of-range negatives silently mean 'neutral' instead of a typed error. Harmless today (app never sends < -1).
findings.recommended_fix: Reject priority/triage < -1 with a typed error.

findings.title: qos_allocate's remainder loop indexes order[] without a bound — negative catalog weights could push the remainder past 3
findings.evidence: 'for i in 0 ..< int(remainder) { caps[order[i]] += 1 }' — remainder is bounded ≤ 2 for non-negative weights (each lane's floor leaves < 1), but a negative weight from a malformed catalog (weights are catalog data; only the bus validates negativity) makes floors negative and remainder unbounded.
findings.detail: The bus rejects negative weights on commands, but balance.json's default_lane_weights/emphasis_preset are only jint-parsed, not range-checked. Requires a corrupted catalog to hit.
findings.recommended_fix: Clamp remainder to len(order) or range-check catalog weights at load.

findings.title: catalogs_hash_sources concatenates the six sources with no length/separator framing — byte-boundary shifts across files collide
findings.evidence: 'mix(&h, src.packet_types); mix(&h, src.pipe_tiers); ...' — FNV-1a over concatenated bytes with no per-file length prefix; 'ab'+'c' vs 'a'+'bc' hash identically.
findings.detail: The catalog_hash is a drift detector, not a security hash — a collision here would silently accept mismatched catalogs in replay/manifest checks. Astronomically unlikely for real JSON, but the framing is free to add.
findings.recommended_fix: Prefix each source with its byte length (or a separator) before mixing.

findings.title: surge_active is cleared by whichever set piece resolves first; overlapping set pieces fire multiple Crisis_Triggered despite the 'fires once' dedup claim
findings.evidence: 'if d.triggered[i] && !d.resolved[i] && tick >= sp.start_tick + sp.duration_ticks { d.resolved[i] = true; c.surge_active = false; ... }' — with two overlapping set pieces, the first to end clears the shared surge_active while the second is still running; each piece fires its own Crisis_Triggered (dedup is per-piece, not per-root-cause E13).
findings.detail: PROTO ships exactly one set piece (streaming_surge), so latent — but the E13 'one active crisis per root cause' contract is implemented as per-set-piece dedup.
findings.recommended_fix: Count active pieces (surge_active = any active), and dedup Crisis_Triggered by root cause across pieces.

findings.title: A node demolished while Strained/Critical resets to Healthy without emitting Ev_Warning_Cleared
findings.evidence: 'if !t.node_alive[i] { c.node_health[i] = .Healthy; continue }' — no Warning_Cleared event; the app's event drain never learns the warning is gone (the HUD reads the snapshot, so visuals are fine; event-stream goldens would differ).
findings.detail: Event-stream contract gap: Warning_Cleared should fire on demolition of a strained node, else event-based assertions on warning resolution are wrong.
findings.recommended_fix: Emit Ev_Warning_Cleared{node} when a dead node's stored health was non-Healthy.

findings.title: A bare 'capture' line with no times is silently accepted as zero captures; intents scheduled after the last tick frame are queued but never applied
findings.evidence: Capture parses trailing times with no minimum; intents with frame > total_frames are appended to the queue and never executed — the audit only counts submissions, so a demo can silently not do what it says.
findings.detail: Demo-authoring footguns: a typo'd capture list or an over-long intent schedule degrades silently instead of failing the parse/run.
findings.recommended_fix: Reject empty capture lists and intents beyond total_frames at parse time.

findings.title: testkit.odin header claims 'NOT used by the game' but the shipped A-key autopilot calls testkit_wire_boot/testkit_autowire; command.odin cites a replay_test.odin that doesn't exist
findings.evidence: testkit.odin: 'testkit.odin — harness/test tooling (NOT used by the game)'; app/run/autopilot.odin calls testkit_wire_boot and testkit_autowire (the A-key demo build). command.odin: 'THE CONVENTION IS PINNED by replay_test.odin' — the file is determinism_test.odin.
findings.detail: Two stale comments that will mislead the next reader; the autopilot-via-testkit pattern also means game code depends on a 'test' file (works, but fragile naming).
findings.recommended_fix: Fix the headers/comments; consider moving the autopilot helpers out of the _testkit name.

findings.title: tier_by_name drops tier_index's ok — an unknown tier silently maps the 1/2/3 keys to tier 0; start_run uses hardcoded 1040×780 map fallback on the first run
findings.evidence: 'tier_by_name :: proc(app: ^App, name: string) -> u16 { idx, _ := pp.tier_index(app.catalogs, name); return idx }'; 'app.map_gen = rnd.map_generate(app.seed, app.view.world_w == 0 ? 1040 : app.view.world_w, app.view.world_h == 0 ? 780 : ...)' — first run always takes the fallback since view_compute hasn't run yet.
findings.detail: Silent tier-0 fallback on a typo'd key; and the first-run map uses hardcoded dims while R-restarts use balance-derived dims — cosmetic inconsistency (map is cosmetic-only), but the tier fallback is a latent misdraw.
findings.recommended_fix: Handle the not-ok case (default to standard or ignore the key); compute the view before the first map_generate.

findings.title: Junction-triage labels 'stream'/'email' plus draw_router puck sizing: integer division flattens ports 1-3; popover labels computed but unused in popover_click
findings.evidence: 'labels := [3]string{"none", "stream", "email"}' in popover_click is never used (the draw side supplies its own); draw_router's port-scaling uses integer division so routers with 1-3 ports render identical, and the formula is overridden for ports ≥ 8.
findings.detail: Cosmetic dead code + a puck-scaling flattening that erases port-count legibility for small routers (canon #14's capacity-scaled visual).
findings.recommended_fix: Remove the unused labels; use float scaling (or a lookup) so 4/8/16 ports read distinctly.

findings.title: Autowire junction tier list {wide, wide} retries the identical command — a deterministic no-op second attempt
findings.evidence: 'tiers := [2]u16{wide, wide}; if !is_j { tiers = {standard, wide} }; for tier in tiers { if submit(...) { break } }' — for junctions both attempts submit wide; if the first fails (span), the second fails identically.
findings.detail: Dead retry for junctions — harmless but signals an intended standard→wide escalation that isn't there.
findings.recommended_fix: tiers := [2]u16{wide} for junctions (or implement the intended escalation).

findings.title: Several tests hardcode class indices and baked catalog tunables into magic numbers; header-only log truncation test is weaker than its name
findings.location: core/flow_test.odin, core/health_test.odin, core/determinism_test.odin (test_action_log_binary_roundtrip 'header-only log must reject' truncates to 8 bytes)
findings.evidence: sla[0]/sla[1], priority=1, u16(0) hardcoded where class_index exists; drain cap 2 / exit 93 / costs 234/360 baked in; the 'header-only' truncation cuts to 8 bytes (magic+version only), not a complete 21-byte header.
findings.detail: Magic-number coupling to catalog tunables makes tests brittle to rebalance (they'd fail on intent, not on bug); the truncation tests still pass but the 'header-only' case is misnamed.
findings.recommended_fix: Read the numbers from the loaded catalog in fixtures; truncate to 21 bytes for the header-only case.

findings.title: jarr_i result slices leak on every catalogs_load; the tracking allocator reports them and the CI gate does not catch it
findings.evidence: jarr_i returns a [dynamic]i64 allocated on context.allocator; callers (jw3, …) never delete it; odin test core's tracking allocator printed '+++ leak ... [catalog.odin:184/242/275/317/339: catalogs_load()]'.
findings.detail: Startup-once allocations, so impact is trivial — but the leak reports pollute every test run and the ODN-18 'no leaks' claim is technically false.
findings.recommended_fix: Allocate jarr_i scratch on the temp allocator (or delete at call sites).

verdict_justification: 2 blockers: a committed 2MB platform-specific build artifact (app.bin, not declared deliberate) and a dead left-click interaction path that makes pipe select, popover dismiss, and demolish unreachable in the mouse-only UI (full routers become permanent dead ends). The determinism spine — the ONE hard blocker per the briefing — is verified INTACT: 40/40 core tests, 5/5 app/run tests, 7/7 harness demos green on a fresh build of the software-rendered raylib shadow, and the replay gate reproduces 3000/3000 + 250/250 ticks bit-for-bit. The T1 fingerprint omits two health fields (warning — completeness gap, not a live break).
